decisions.reason: As a close-to-core finishing product in a growing industry, it likely remains near acceptable aspiration levels, so management would keep it unless clearer evidence of weak demand appears.

Because this UV spot varnishing system is more distant from the established offer and has had time to prove itself, it faces a higher risk of falling short of aspirations, but its flagship role and strategic fit still justify retention for now.

This sheet preparation module fits tightly with the firm's modular postpress workflow, so boundedly rational management would see little reason to drop it without explicit negative performance signals.
The B2 multifinisher remains closely aligned with the firm's core automation direction and flagship positioning, making continued support more likely than withdrawal.
A hybrid saddle stitcher sits within the firm's traditional booklet-making business, and absent signs of underperformance organizational slack makes keeping it more likely than dropping it.
The folding add-on unit already showed early customer adoption and complements installed finishing lines, which lowers the chance that management judges it below aspiration and removes it.
